answer: A farm running 142 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the garden stake is held until the quartz settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the trellis audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 16% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
